Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Can I judge a religion by how its people act?

A Gospel image and a Quranic one agree: look at the fruit. The hard part: which fruit, and who is the tree?

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ٢٤ تُؤْتِىٓ أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍۭ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا ۗ وَيَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ٢٥ وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ٱجْتُثَّتْ مِن فَوْقِ ٱلْأَرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ٢٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you not considered how Allāh presents an example, [making] a good word like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches [high] in the sky? It produces its fruit all the time, by permission of its Lord. And Allāh presents examples for the people that perhaps they will be reminded. And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, not having any stability.

Quran · Ibrahim 14:24-26

Translation

He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.

Original · Hebrew

וְֽהָיָ֗ה כְּעֵץ֮ שָׁת֪וּל עַֽל־פַּלְגֵ֫י מָ֥יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר פִּרְי֨וֹ ׀ יִתֵּ֬ן בְּעִתּ֗וֹ וְעָלֵ֥הוּ לֹֽא־יִבּ֑וֹל וְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יַצְלִֽיחַ׃

the Psalms · 1:3

World English Bible

Here is a test older than any of us: a tree shows what it is by what it bears. Readers of the Gospels know it from the teaching of Jesus. This image makes the same move with words. A good word is a tree with deep roots and high branches, giving fruit in every season. A rotten word has no roots and cannot stand. So the test is not how a message sounds. It is what it does over time, in real people, in hard seasons.

A question for you

What would count as good fruit, for you?

If you sayHonesty and mercy in ordinary people.
ThenThen you have a standard that belongs to no single religion, which makes it fair to use on all of them.
If you sayJustice for the weak.
ThenA demanding test, and one that history can speak to. It will give mixed results for every group, Muslims included, and all of that belongs in the weighing.
If you sayPeace in the person who follows it.
ThenThat is real, and it can be seen. Its limit is that peace can come from other sources too, so it counts best alongside the rest.

Part 2 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ٢ كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allāh is that you say what you do not do.

Quran · As-Saff 61:2-3

the Gospel (Matthew) · 23:3

World English Bible

﴿أَتَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Do you order righteousness of the people and forget[25] yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?

Translator's notes

[25] Make exceptions of.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:44

Translation

You therefore who teach another, don’t you teach yourself? You who preach that a man shouldn’t steal, do you steal?

Original · Ancient Greek

ὁ οὖν διδάσκων ἕτερον σεαυτὸν οὐ διδάσκεις; ὁ κηρύσσων μὴ κλέπτειν κλέπτεις;

Romans · 2:21

World English Bible

Now the hard part, at full strength. You have seen cruelty, greed and abuse from religious people, Muslims among them. If fruit is the test, why is that not the end of it? Because two things are being judged: what a teaching produces in those who live by it, and what people do while wearing its name. A person who breaks a rule is no evidence that the rule is bad. This verse is addressed to believers themselves, and asks why they say what they do not do.

A question for you

When a follower behaves badly, what does that show, in your view?

If you sayThat the teaching failed.
ThenSometimes it does. If a teaching makes people worse the more closely they follow it, that counts against it. The question is whether they followed it.
If you sayThat the person failed.
ThenOften so. But if that answer is always available, the test can never fail, and that is a fair worry.
If you sayI cannot separate the two.
ThenMany people who have been hurt cannot, and that is honest. There is a question written for you.

Part 3 of 3

﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:97

Translation

Behold, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith.

Original · Hebrew

הִנֵּ֣ה עֻפְּלָ֔ה לֹא־יָשְׁרָ֥ה נַפְשׁ֖וֹ בּ֑וֹ וְצַדִּ֖יק בֶּאֱמוּנָת֥וֹ יִחְיֶֽה׃

Habakkuk · 2:4

World English Bible

A fair test needs rules, or it only confirms what you already think. Three rules help. Judge a teaching by those who follow it most closely, not by the loudest. Look across long stretches and hard times, not one bright decade. Use the same measure on every tradition, your own included. Then ask what the text itself promises. This verse promises a good life to any man or woman who joins faith and good deeds. That can be watched for.

A question for you

Which of the three rules would be hardest for you to keep?

If you sayJudging my own side by the same measure.
ThenThat is the hardest for nearly everyone. The text asks it first of its own readers.
If you sayLooking at the best followers, not the worst.
ThenAnyone who has been hurt has good reason to find this hard. It does not need doing today.
If you sayWaiting long enough to see.
ThenA slow test suits a slow question. It also means that no one is hurrying you.
